pr_title: usb: Add macro for user defined string descriptors
pr_body:
The new macro USBD_STRING_DESCR_USER_DEFINE works like
USBD_STRING_DESCR_DEFINE with the exception of being
ordered strictly after it. The new macro is needed to
ensures that user defined string descriptors can be added
without disturbing the order of string descriptors
defined by the usb subsystem.

Fixes  #41017

issue_context.title: USB string descriptors can be re-ordered causing corruption and out-of-bounds-write
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
While trying to implement a USB video device I encountered
unexpected errors in `dmesg` when plugging in the device.

I managed to to track the problem to the single string descriptor I had
defined. I believe my string descriptor was placed before the other string descriptors
(`string_descr` in `usb_descriptor.c`) by the linker, causing the `usb_fix_descriptor`
routine to break in ways I don't yet understand.
I have created a PR https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/41014  that fixes my issue by disambiguating the order
between string descriptor zero and other string descriptors.

**To Reproduce**
Since the issue is with under specified section ordering I have not
been able to find a way to reproduce this with any in-tree boards or samples.

I'm working on my USB video class driver out-of-tree application,
that might affect the link order.

The following config options were helpful in discovering the cause:
```
CONFIG_USB_DEVICE_LOG_LEVEL_DBG=y
CONFIG_LOG_BUFFER_SIZE=4096
```

comments:
I've convinced myself that the corruption happens when another string descriptor is placed before the string descriptors in `struct usb_string_desription string_descr` and their indices are shifted so `usb_fix_ascii_sn_string_descriptor` is called with the product string descriptor instead of the serial number descriptor.

In the default config the product string is smaller than the serial number, so `memcpy` writes out of bounds, overwriting the `bLength` field of the next descriptor, corrupting the descriptor structure.

I found confirmation in `zephyr.map`. In the snippet below you can see that the string descriptor (identifiable by the section ` .usb.descriptor_primary.4`) that I defined in `usb_video.c` is placed before the string descriptors defined by `usb_descriptor.c`.

```
 *(SORT_BY_ALIGNMENT(.usb.descriptor))
 *(SORT_BY_NAME(SORT_BY_ALIGNMENT(.usb.descriptor*)))
 .usb.descriptor_primary.0
                0x0000000020000190       0x1b zephyr/libzephyr.a(usb_descriptor.c.obj)
 .usb.descriptor_primary.1.0
                0x00000000200001ab       0x9f app/libapp.a(usb_video.c.obj)
 .usb.descriptor_primary.4
                0x000000002000024a        0x8 app/libapp.a(usb_video.c.obj)
 .usb.descriptor_primary.4
                0x0000000020000252       0x44 zephyr/libzephyr.a(usb_descriptor.c.obj)
 .usb.descriptor_primary.5
                0x0000000020000296        0x2 zephyr/libzephyr.a(usb_descriptor.c.obj)
                0x0000000020000298                __usb_descriptor_end = .
```

For clarification, string descriptors are optional. There is no straightforward support in the current USB device support for the string descriptors defined in class or application code. Event with #41014, there is no solution to avoid indexes conflict as they are not part of string descriptor and we do not have a container for that.

According to the USB Video Class Specification there is one mandatory string descriptor. The rest are optional as you say.

Can you clarify what you mean about index conflicts? I don't currently have a need to explicitly control the indexes. From my (very) limited understanding of the USB protocol there is no need to control the string descriptor ordering (aside from index 0). You just have to make sure to point to the right string from your other descriptors and it seems like `usb_get_str_descriptor_idx` can be used for that purpose.

review_comments:
Better the other way around with minimal changes, just:
```diff
diff --git a/include/usb/usb_device.h b/include/usb/usb_device.h
index 8884c8afbbe..83abab6755f 100644
--- a/include/usb/usb_device.h
+++ b/include/usb/usb_device.h
@@ -60,8 +60,10 @@ extern "C" {
        static __in_section(usb, descriptor_##p, 3) __used __aligned(1)
 #define USBD_STRING_DESCR_DEFINE(p) \
        static __in_section(usb, descriptor_##p, 4) __used __aligned(1)
-#define USBD_TERM_DESCR_DEFINE(p) \
+#define USBD_STRING_DESCR_USER_DEFINE(p) \
        static __in_section(usb, descriptor_##p, 5) __used __aligned(1)
+#define USBD_TERM_DESCR_DEFINE(p) \
+       static __in_section(usb, descriptor_##p, 6) __used __aligned(1)
 
 /*
  * This macro should be used to place the struct usb_cfg_data
```

Please revise you commit message, among others: "Without this fix, the order between individual string descriptors is undefined." is not correct. The order is well defined, you just need to understand how it works.

What would be a better wording? The order might not be "undefined" per se, but from what I can tell there is currently no explicit constraint to ensure that the "initial" string descriptors are really placed first.
Something like: "Add a new macro to define string descriptors in the user code more easily with the respect for the correct order."

Sorry. The project where I needed this fix kind of fell to the wayside. I have changed the implementation like @jfischer-no suggested, and updated the commit message & PR description.
